newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Metal Manufactures sees Asia projects.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Metal Manufactures sees Asia projects.

text.p: Metal Manufactures Ltd said on Monday it had a number of projects on the drawing board for its new Asia-Pacific optical cable joint venture with parent company BICC Plc and U.S.-based Corning Inc.
Metal Manufactures said the joint venture, to be known as BICCOR, would be 60 percent owned by BICC Cables Asia-Pacific Pte Ltd and 40 percent by Corning.
BICC Cables Asia-Pacific is a 50/50 joint venture between Metal Manufactures and BICC Plc, which owns about 62 percent of the Australian building materials and cable group.
Metal Manufactures managing director Glenn Dudley said BICCOR would focus on developing optical cable manufacturing facilities in the region.
Funds would be invested on a project by project basis, with the main customers for optical fibre expected to be the region's telecoms.
"There's an enormous amount of growth in telecommunications around the world, but we think in particular in Asia-Pacific where there is very little optical fibre at this point," he told Reuters.
Dudley said the company had two or three ventures on the drawing board, but arrangements had not been finalised.
BICCOR would aim to set up local manufacturing facilities in each country, with a typical project involving investment of US$25 million to US$50 million, he said.
The joint venture would allow quicker acceptance for all parties throughout the Asia-Pacific region, he said.
Metal Manufactures and Corning have had an 11-year relationship in a 50/50 joint venture which manufactures optical fibre in Melbourne.
